name: Venet & Venetbahn
kurzbeschreibung: Mount Venet (2,208 m Krahberg) above Landeck/Zams offers 360-degree panoramas of over 80 alpine peaks, Tyrol’s highest observatory, and Tobi’s adventure trail.
beschreibung:
Overview

Venet (2,208 m at the Krahberg peak) is the prominent local mountain presiding over the Landeck-Zams-Fließ valley basin, revered by alpine enthusiasts as one of the finest panoramic summits in the Central Alps. From the expansive crest of the Krahberg, visitors are greeted by an astounding 360-degree view taking in over 80 alpine giants, including the glaciated Wildspitze, King Ortler, the Swiss Silvretta, and Germany's Zugspitze. On clear days, the extraordinary vista extends far across national borders. Thanks to its sun-drenched and exposed position, the summit hosts Tyrol's highest astronomical observatory, complete with a modern solar telescope. In summer, the massif is a versatile playground for hiking, paragliding, and mountain biking, whilst in winter it transforms into a sunny, family-friendly ski area with delightful alpine huts.

Route & Requirements

The modern Venet cable car whisks guests from Zams straight up to the mountain station at 2,208 metres in just a few minutes. Encircling the top station is a gentle, barrier-free panorama path leading to the viewing deck and the observatory (around 20 minutes' walk), ideally suited for pushchairs and seniors. Younger guests adore "Tobi’s Erlebnisweg", filled with interactive activity points and balance challenges, while cosy sun loungers along the trail invite relaxation with mountain views. Ambitious hikers can undertake the challenging Venet ridge traverse across Glanderspitz (2,512 m), which requires sure-footedness, freedom from vertigo, and alpine equipment. Mountain bikers will find signposted singletrails down to the valley. Normal walking shoes suffice around the summit, whereas high-ankle mountain boots are essential for ridge excursions.

Visit & Arrival

The Venet cable car operates in summer from late May to mid-October daily between 08:30 and 17:00 (winter operations from December to March). Round-trip tickets are around €25.00 for adults, with attractive savings for TirolWest Card holders. The valley station is located directly in Zams, providing a large complimentary car and coach park. Rail travellers arrive conveniently at the Landeck-Zams long-distance railway station, reaching the cable car in a 10-minute walk or via local shuttle bus.

Tips

Book an evening stargazing tour at the Venet Observatory on clear nights to gaze upon distant nebulae and planets through high-powered telescope lenses. Afterwards, sample traditional Tyrolean Kaspressknödel cheese dumplings on the sun-drenched terrace of the panorama summit restaurant.
